item.content:encoded:
Cristopher Sánchez turned his back as Don Mattingly walked to the mound. Sánchez, with his pitch count at 98 in the seventh inning, had a runner on first and one out. But Mattingly wanted to go to rookie Alex McFarlane, his most trusted high leverage arm outside of Jhoan Duran.
Sánchez stared into center field. He eventually looked over his shoulder and gave the ball to Mattingly. He screamed as he walked back to the dugout and shook his head as he watched the remainder of the inning from the dugout.
McFarlane, with two outs and two runners on, blew three fastballs right by Juan Soto for the final out of the inning. He may have gone back out for the eighth, but the Phillies scored three runs in the top half of the inning. Mattingly instead went to Chase Shugart in the eighth and José Alvarado in the ninth. Both relievers threw scoreless innings. All three helped preserve Sánchez’s league-leading 18th win of the season and a 7-2 Phillies win over the New York Mets on a rainy Sunday afternoon at Citi Field.
Sánchez may have been perturbed by what he perceived to be an early pull, but he pitched well when he was in the game. That’s all that really matters for the Phillies, who desperately need the best version of Sánchez to show up next week in the wild card round.
After allowing 18 hits in his last two starts, Sánchez bounced back. After doing a deep dive on his recent mechanical issues, Sánchez limited traffic on the bases and had his signature changeup going.
His next scheduled start is Saturday at home against the Tampa Bay Rays. He’ll have to pitch if the Phillies haven’t clinched yet. With the win, the Phillies’ magic number to make the postseason is 3. Seeding, and an opportunity to host the wild card series, could be on the line.
If they do clinch in the next few days, the Phillies could opt to rest him and get him ready for the postseason. The Phillies could also move his start up a day to Friday with the off day on Monday and have him pitch on regular rest for Game 2 of a potential wild card series. How the Phillies manage their rotation over the last weekend will be interesting. Both Sánchez and Zack Wheeler are lined up to pitch the final two games of the year. They will have to find someone who can eat innings.
The Phillies broke the game wide open in the eighth on a bases-clearing triple by Justin Crawford. Prior to Crawford’s big hit, all of the Phillies offense came in the first three innings. They scored twice in the first on a Luis Arraez sacrifice fly and an RBI single from Alec Bohm. The two runs in the third broke an odd streak of five consecutive games in which the Phillies scored exactly three runs.
The Phillies will head back to Philadelphia for the start of the final homestand of the regular season on Tuesday against the Milwaukee Brewers. Pending the results of the Diamondbacks vs. Yankees game, the Phillies could clinch at home as early as Tuesday night. Wheeler will get the start for the Phillies in the opening game.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

20 Sep 2026, 17:10 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Brad Penner)
The New York Mets spent the first half of their final homestand being reminded of what they were missing without Pete Alonso.
Carson Benge is closing the home schedule by providing the Mets a hint of what they'll have for the foreseeable future.
Benge and the Mets will look to end their home slate on a winning note on Sunday afternoon when they face the Philadelphia Phillies in the finale of a four-game series.
Mets right-hander Jonah Tong (2-1, 3.43 ERA) will oppose Phillies left-hander Cristopher Sanchez (17-6, 2.93).
Benge helped the Mets hurt the Phillies' chances of being in the top wild-card spot in the National League on Saturday, when the rookie outfielder homered among his three hits in a 10-3 victory.
The win was the second straight for the Mets (71-84) following a five-game losing streak that included a three-game sweep by Alonso and the Baltimore Orioles.
Alonso set the Mets' all-time record with 264 homers before signing with the Orioles as a free agent in December. He received standing ovations before every at-bat in Monday's 2-1 Baltimore win before he hit his 300th career homer in the ninth inning of Tuesday's 7-5 victory in 11 innings. The slugger went deep again in Wednesday's 7-1 rout.
But Benge nudged ahead of Alonso in one category in the Mets' record book Saturday, when his three hits gave him 156 this season, breaking the rookie high of 155 set by Alonso in 2019.
Benge's record-breaking performance is doubly impressive considering he opened the season with just 17 hits in his first 90 at-bats through April 30. He is batting .292 since May 1.
'I came in knowing I belonged,' Benge said. 'It was kind of rough there in the beginning, but (he was) sticking to my path and grinding out every day and now finally showing others that I finally belong here, too.'
Benge's big day may have made the playoff path more difficult for the Phillies (85-70), who have lost 10 of their last 16 games to fall into the NL's third wild-card spot.
The Phillies are one game behind the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres, who earned wins later Saturday over the Cincinnati Reds and Miami Marlins, respectively. The final wild card will open the playoffs at the No. 3 seed, likely the NL East-leading Atlanta Braves, who are four games behind the Los Angeles Dodgers in the race for the second seed and final bye in the first round.
The Phillies have a four-game wild-card edge over the Arizona Diamondbacks, who beat the New York Yankees on Saturday night.
'I just don't think these guys are going to sit back and panic,' Philadelphia interim manager Don Mattingly said. 'We're in a better spot than a lot of teams, so I think we're positive on it. Honestly, we know what we're capable of.'
Tong didn't factor into the decision in his most recent start last Monday, when he allowed an unearned run over six innings in the Mets' 2-1 loss to the Orioles. He has yet to face the Phillies in his career.
Sanchez took the defeat Tuesday after giving up five runs over 6 1/3 innings in Philadelphia's 6-3 loss to the Washington Nationals. He is 4-4 with a 3.97 ERA in 13 career games (10 starts) against the Mets.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Those following the Major League Baseball postseason picture will see and hear the term “earn” frequently mentioned within the coming days, which isn’t exactly the word that comes to mind upon looking at the standings.
Outside of the 60-game 2020 season, we’ve never seen a losing team make the playoffs. Depending on how the next eight days play out, there could be four American League teams that finish with 81 or fewer wins yet qualify for the playoffs.
The easiest way to keep tabs on how close teams are to clinching is by looking at magic numbers. The formula to calculate a magic number is as follows, per MLB.com:
- Games remaining +1 - (Losses by second place team - losses by first place team)
American League standings and playoff picture
For all intents and purposes, the Red Sox have clinched a playoff berth; they entered Saturday with their magic number sitting at two, and they’re so far ahead in the Wild Card standings that they’re all but locked into a first-round matchup with the Yankees. It’d be the fourth time in less than a decade these two have met in the playoffs, and the Red Sox look to avenge last year’s Wild Card Series loss.
The AL Central and AL West are, shall we say, messy. Houston holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over Texas and is only two games back of Cleveland for the AL’s No. 2 seed. Meanwhile, the White Sox have a one-game lead over the Rangers for the final Wild Card berth, and we could realistically see three of those teams make the postseason with a losing record.
| Team | Record | Games back |
|---|---|---|
| Tampa Bay Rays | 93-60 | -- |
| Cleveland Guardians | 79-75 | 14.5 |
| Houston Astros | 77-77 | 16.5 |
| New York Yankees | 89-64 (WC) | 4 |
| Boston Red Sox | 84-70 (WC) | 9.5 |
| Chicago White Sox | 78-76 (WC) | 15.5 |
| Texas Rangers | 77-77 (OUT) | 16.5 |
| Toronto Blue Jays | 76-78 (OUT) | 16.5 |
| Baltimore Orioles | 75-79 (OUT) | 18.5 |
If the regular season ended today, here's a look at what the AL Wild Card round matchups would look like.
- Bye: (1) Tampa Bay Rays
- Bye: (2) Cleveland Guardians
- (3) Houston Astros vs. (6) Chicago White Sox
- (4) New York Yankees vs. (5) Boston Red Sox
National League standings and playoff picture
The only thing that’s changed in the National League is how crowded the Wild Card race has become. Barring a collapse over the season’s final week, we’re all but assured of the Cubs, Phillies, and Padres being the three Wild Card teams. That’s been the case for most of September, as has the Braves being the No. 3 seed and NL East champions.
How the seeding will work, though, is where things get interesting. The Cubs, Phillies, and Padres all began Saturday at 85-69, and they’d be seeded in that order; No. 4 Chicago would host No. 5 Philadelphia, and No. 6 San Diego would play at Atlanta.
Unfortunately for the Phillies, they close the regular season with a six-game homestand against the Brewers and Rays. Both teams are still fighting for the top seeds in their respective leagues, so don’t expect them to go lightly on Don Mattingly’s club.
| Team | Record | Games back |
|---|---|---|
| Milwaukee Brewers | 93-60 | -- |
| Los Angeles Dodgers | 79-75 | 2.0 |
| Atlanta Braves | 77-77 | 6.0 |
| Chicago Cubs | 85-69 (WC) | 11.0 |
| Philadelphia Phillies | 85-69 (WC) | 11.0 |
| San Diego Padres | 85-69 (WC) | 11.0 |
| Arizona Diamondbacks | 80-74 (OUT) | 16.0 |
If the regular season ended today, here’s a look at what the NL Wild Card round matchups would look like.
- Bye: (1) Milwaukee Brewers
- Bye: (2) Los Angeles Dodgers
- (3) Atlanta Braves vs. (6) San Diego Padres
- (4) Chicago Cubs vs. (5) Philadelphia Phillies
MLB magic numbers: Which AL teams are closest to clinching a playoff spot?
| Team | Magic number | Elimination number |
|---|---|---|
| Tampa Bay Rays | CLINCHED | -- |
| Cleveland Guardians | 7 | -- |
| Houston Astros | 8 | -- |
| New York Yankees | CLINCHED | -- |
| Boston Red Sox | 2 | -- |
| Chicago White Sox | 7 | 8 |
| Texas Rangers | | 8 |
| Toronto Blue Jays | | 6 |
| Baltimore Orioles | | 6 |
| Detroit Tigers | | 3 |
| Seattle Mariners | | 4 |
| Minnesota Twins | | 3 |
| Kansas City Royals | -- | ELIMINATED |
| Athletics | -- | ELIMINATED |
| Los Angeles Angels | -- | ELIMINATED |
As we said, half of the AL playoff picture has essentially already been determined. Only three games separate the White Sox and Orioles, who are still mathematically alive despite entering Saturday with a 75-79 record. Let’s also not forget about the 76-78 Blue Jays, who are only two games back of the White Sox.
We recently referenced the 2008 Yankees, who missed the playoffs at 89-73 and watched the Dodgers win the NL West with 84 wins. If we created a portal and grabbed that Yankees team, they’d be the AL’s No. 4 seed if the playoffs began tomorrow, and it wouldn’t be close. Great job, all.
But hey, we objectively love chaos, so we’re in the minority in loving the AL playoff picture.
MLB magic numbers: Which NL teams are closest to clinching a playoff spot?
There’s not much else to say about the National League playoff picture. The teams that haven’t officially locked up a playoff berth should do so within the coming days, and the Diamondbacks’ tragic number dropped to four following Friday night’s loss to the Yankees.
| Team | Magic number | Elimination number |
|---|---|---|
| Milwaukee Brewers | CLINCHED | -- |
| Los Angeles Dodgers | CLINCHED | -- |
| Atlanta Braves | CLINCHED | -- |
| Chicago Cubs | 3 | -- |
| Philadelphia Phillies | 4 | -- |
| San Diego Padres | 4 | -- |
| Arizona Diamondbacks | -- | 4 |
| Pittsburgh Pirates | -- | ELIMINATED |
| Miami Marlins | -- | ELIMINATED |
| St. Louis Cardinals | -- | ELIMINATED |
| Washington Nationals | -- | ELIMINATED |
| Cincinnati Reds | -- | ELIMINATED |
| New York Mets | -- | ELIMINATED |
| San Francisco Giants | -- | ELIMINATED |
| Colorado Rockies | -- | ELIMINATED |
It’s hard not to feel bad for the Rockies. Despite not blowing up their roster at the trade deadline, they're 13-31 since Aug. 1, and they haven't had a winning streak longer than four games all year. Warren Schaeffer’s club is two losses away from its fourth consecutive 100-loss season, and they’ve been outscored by nearly 200 runs.
But considering they went 43-119 last year, this technically means they’ve made significant progress. Yikes.

MLB: ¡Edmundo Sosa arde y Don Mattingly lo frena!
- 19/09/2026 11:14
El técnico no cambiará sus planes terminando la temporada.
El buen momento ofensivo que atraviesa el panameño Edmundo Sosa no es suficiente para alterar el plan de los Filis de Filadelfia en la recta final de la temporada.
El mánager Don Mattingly decidió mantener su alineación, aun cuando Sosa atraviesa una importante recuperación ofensiva y ha elevado considerablemente su producción durante las últimas semanas.
La decisión generó preguntas, tomando en cuenta el rendimiento reciente del infielder, pero Mattingly dejó claro que, de cara a los playoffs, el equipo no pretende modificar drásticamente su fórmula.
“Pensé en mantener a Sosa en el equipo, pero me gusta la consistencia de seguir haciendo lo que hacemos”, explicó Mattingly.
“Hemos estado haciendo esto durante todo el año. Ya nos quedan los partidos que nos quedan. Creo que cambiar muchas cosas y alejarnos de lo que hacemos transmite pánico, y entonces nos metemos en un lío”, agregó.
El estratega también explicó que las decisiones sobre la participación de Sosa están relacionadas con los emparejamientos y las características de los lanzadores rivales.
“Tenemos que permitir que nuestros jugadores hagan lo que mejor saben hacer. Y también con Sosa, hay que buscar el emparejamiento adecuado. Depende del tipo de lanzador que sea. Algunas de las decisiones que tomas con él se basan en su estilo, su forma de atacar y cosas así. De nuevo, pensamos que ese era un mejor lugar para Marsh en el montículo”, agregó.
Sosa cambia el rumbo
Mientras los Filis mantienen su plan, Sosa ha dado un giro importante a su temporada con el bate.
Comenzó agosto con un OPS de apenas .587, una cifra que reflejaba las dificultades ofensivas que había enfrentado durante buena parte de la campaña.
Sin embargo, su producción ha ido en ascenso y ahora su OPS se ubica en .708, superando nuevamente la barrera de .700 por primera vez desde comienzos de mayo.
El repunte llega en un momento clave, cuando los Filis se acercan a la postemporada y cada decisión sobre la alineación adquiere mayor relevancia.
Sosa, además de aportar con el bate, continúa siendo una pieza de utilidad para Filadelfia por su capacidad para desempeñarse en diferentes posiciones del cuadro interior.
La postura de Mattingly deja un mensaje claro: los Filis no piensan apartarse de la fórmula que han utilizado durante la temporada, incluso cuando jugadores como Sosa atraviesan momentos ofensivos positivos.

item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies opened a series with the New York Mets on Thursday night and won the game 3-0 to improve to 85-68 overall.
However, in spite of the victory, the team dealt with a notable injury out of their bullpen to right-handed reliever Jonathan Bowlan, who has been a workhorse for the Phillies this year.
He exited the eighth inning after recording two strikeouts with a reported groin strain.
Don Mattingly Makes Honest Statement on Injury
While it’s still unknown exactly the extent of the injury and how long Bowlan may be out, Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly made an honest statement after losing a key arm out of the pen.
“Paul said right groin tightness, so we’ll reevaluate tomorrow to see where he’s at,” Mattingly said. “We’ll talk about it more tomorrow but at this point you just… I don’t want to be cold hearted but you got to move on and you have to find a way to fill that spot. Which is not necessarily easy to do, but that means other guys got to step up, that’s all.”
“That means other guys got to step up, that’s all.”
Don Mattingly says other arms will need to rise to the occasion if Jonathan Bowlan misses time. pic.twitter.com/5FnoNJ2Mjv
— NBC Sports Philadelphia (@NBCSPhilly) September 18, 2026
Bowlan’s 2026 Season
In his fourth MLB season, but first with the Phillies after spending the last three years with the Kansas City Royals, Bowlan has been one of the best arms out of Philadelphia’s pen.
He’s appeared in 59 games, and across 56.1 innings pitched, he holds a 2-2 record with a 3.36 ERA, 73 strikeouts, and two saves.
Looking at the Phillies
Philadelphia is still trying to chase the Atlanta Braves in the NL East, trailing them by 4.0 games with nine regular-season games remaining.
The Phillies also want the top Wild Card spot, which would give them home-field advantage in a best-of-three Wild Card Series, but they remain tied with the Chicago Cubs for that spot.

item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies are using their newest pitching addition to reshape their weekend plans as they push toward the postseason.
Phillies manager Don Mattingly confirmed that right-hander José Urquidy will be active for Friday's game and used in a bullpen game against the New York Mets. The move allows Philadelphia to keep top pitching prospect Andrew Painter on his normal schedule for Saturday.
Urquidy was claimed off waivers from the Chicago White Sox on Thursday. He gives the Phillies another option to cover innings while the pitching staff deals with the absence of Jesús Luzardo.
The Phillies also transferred right-hander Caleb Kilian to the 60-day injured list to clear a 40-man roster spot for Urquidy.
The 31-year-old has spent most of the season working in a long-relief role. He threw 22.2 innings for the White Sox, posting a 4.37 ERA, 15 strikeouts and a 1.19 WHIP.
Urquidy has also pitched for the Pittsburgh Pirates this season and owns a 4.08 ERA across his MLB career. He previously faced Philadelphia during the 2022 World Series with the Houston Astros.
Painter will now get the extra day before making his Saturday start. The rookie has made 23 appearances, including 21 starts, and has logged 115.1 innings with 100 strikeouts and 43 walks.
The results have been uneven, with Painter carrying a 5.54 ERA, but he showed what he can provide in his most recent outing. He allowed one run over five innings against the Atlanta Braves on Sept. 13.
The timing of the move is also important for Philadelphia's bullpen. Urquidy can absorb innings Friday and help keep high-leverage relievers such as Jhoan Duran from being overworked with the postseason approaching.
Urquidy will not be eligible for Philadelphia's postseason roster because he was acquired after the Sept. 1 deadline. His immediate value is giving Mattingly another arm to navigate the final games of the regular season.
The Phillies entered Friday trailing the Cubs (85-68) by a half-game for the top Wild Card position. With the regular season winding down, the club is clearly prioritizing pitching availability and keeping its key arms on schedule.
